title: POC scoping - Cobalt Systems - integration planning
summary: POC scoping focused on integration plan: use Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs, validate latency/cost tradeoffs with benchmark runs, define success criteria (latency p95, accuracy on prompt set, cost per 1k tokens), and agree timeline for a 3-week pilot including benchmark window and deliverables.
next_steps: Redwood to share POC pricing and dedicated pilot agreement
Redwood SE to run baseline benchmark (1000 requests) and share results
Customer to provide canonical prompt set and sample tool schema
Customer to enable temporary access to staging data endpoint
action_items: Priya Nair: run baseline perf benchmark against hosted endpoint (1k requests, varied seq lengths) - due 2026-08-05
Marcus Li: share canonical prompt set (50 prompts covering edge cases) and sample logs - due 2026-08-02
Jared Kim: send POC SOW + pricing and security pack (SOC2, encryption, KMS notes) - due 2026-07-31
Dana Park: confirm network/VPC requirements for private pilot and provide infra contact - due 2026-08-04
transcript:
[00:00] Jared (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. agenda for today quick scoping for the POC, success criteria, workload, and how we'll integrate - sdk, openai compat, function calling etc.
[00:18] Lena (Cobalt CTO): yeah thanks, we have a hard deadline to show value to ops by mid-september so timeline is tight. main use case is automated incident triage and suggested runbooks, plus a summarization flow for post-incident reviews.
[00:35] Marcus (ML): to add, we will need structured outputs for the triage results (severity, probable cause, recommended runbook id) — that structured JSON must be strict cause it feeds our downstream automation.
[00:52] Priya (Redwood SE): got it, structured outputs are something we support via JSON-schema style responses and function-calling emulation. we also offer an openai-compatible endpoint so integration is pretty straightforward. small warning sometimes our feature names get transcribed differently, like Redwood Dedicated becomes "Redwood Dedictated" in notes ha.
[01:10] Dana (Infra): on the infra side we need to know if we'll use hosted or dedicated. security wants VPC options and KMS for keys. also latency SLOs are important — this needs to be realtimeish.
[01:28] Jared: for the POC we usually recommend starting with hosted openai-compatible endpoints to iterate fast, then move to Dedicated if throughput/cost requires. success criteria proposal: p95 latency < 600ms for short queries, accuracy of triage labels >= 88% on your evaluation prompts, and cost under $Y per 1k tokens (we'll fill in pricing).
[01:49] Owen (PM): 600ms p95 sounds reasonable, what's typical for a 250-token response?
[01:56] Priya: depends on model selection and batching. for a 250-token completion on our curated models you should expect 350-700ms p95 when hosted, lower if you run on Dedicated GPU pools or use quantized variants. we will run benchmarks to validate.
[02:15] Marcus: what's the concurrency we should test? production will see spikes up to 50 rps but sustained maybe 12-15 rps.
[02:24] Priya: ok note that. for benchmarking we'll run profiles at 5, 15, 50 rps with sequence lengths 64, 250, 800 tokens to capture extremes.
[02:40] Lena: also we need deterministic structured outputs because our automation will parse them — function calling or strict json response?
[02:48] Samir (Redwood Solutions Eng): function calling maps well here — we can return typed outputs and even validate against your schema. If you want to use straight completions we recommend a lightweight post-processor and strong JSON schema prompts. we can share examples.
[03:05] Owen: we mostly prefer OpenAI-compatible SDKs since our backend is already wired to openai client calls. how close is Redwood's compatibility?
[03:12] Priya: it's intentionally close — same request/response shapes, same function calling surface. a couple of non-breaking differences on headers and rate-limit responses, but we provide SDK wrappers for node/python to make it drop-in.
[03:25] Dana: what about streaming responses? we need partial payloads for logs.
[03:30] Priya: streaming supported; and we support chunked detection so your ingest can start earlier. caveat on batching — streaming plus heavy batching can increase overall latency per request on some workloads. we'll show tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[03:50] Marcus: token accounting question — how do you measure tokens for hybrid prompt+tool calls? we use that to estimate cost.
[03:58] Priya: our billing uses token-equivalent measurement similar to openai, prompt+completion tokens counted. for function calls the call payload is included. for POC we'll provide a cost estimator spreadsheet from your sample prompts.
[04:15] Lena: security check — we require SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO (SAML). is that all supported?
[04:23] Jared: yes we have SOC2, KMS options for Dedicated/Private, audit logs with token-level traces in the console, and SAML SSO. we'll attach the security pack.
[04:34] Owen: timeline, what's realistic? we have a stakeholder demo target of 2026-09-15.
[04:40] Jared: with that target I'd propose a 3-week pilot: week 0 onboarding + prompt set + infra, week 1 run benchmarks & iterate, week 2 validate quality and handoff to ops. that lands us comfortably before mid-september for a demo.
[04:58] Lena: ok that aligns. what does onboarding require? credentials, sample data, network access, and a contact who can approve a staging token?
[05:08] Jared: yes, we'll need a staging API key and your sample prompt set and expected labels. if you want a VPC pilot we'll coordinate networking with Dana.
[05:16] Marcus: how do we validate accuracy? can you run our evaluation harnesses?
[05:21] Priya: yes we can run your eval harness — please share the 50-100 labelled examples; we'll run accuracy, precision/recall on triage labels, and a separate pass for summarization quality (ROUGE / human sample checks).
[05:37] Dana: for Private/on-prem we have some air-gapped requirements — is that feasible for later phases?
[05:44] Samir: absolutely, Private deployment is more involved but supported; for the POC we recommend hosted with VPC peering or Dedicated to keep things moving.
[06:00] Marcus: about structured schemas can you show an example of function calling for triage?
[06:05] Priya: sure here's an example we will share in the follow-up: a function signature with fields severity:string, cause_codes: [string], runbook_id:string, confidence:float; Redwood will return JSON matching that shape or use function-calling to constrain the answer.
[06:24] Lena: and if the model returns bad json mid-stream? we need a retry strategy.
[06:28] Priya: we have response validation on the client sdk; if the shape doesn't match we can attempt a single deterministic re-call with additional context. for critical flows we use a lightweight verifier lambda before automation consumes it.
[06:45] Jared: ok let's talk benchmarks specifics — priya will run baseline on hosted model A and model B (smaller quantized variant) with 1k requests each at different seq lengths. we'll capture p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and tail latencies.
[07:02] Priya: yep and we'll provide a spreadsheet with cost projections for both hosted and extrapolated Dedicated numbers. will also measure batching effects: batch sizes 1, 4, 8.
[07:15] Marcus: are you able to mimic our traffic pattern? we have diurnal spikes and occasional bursts from CI.
[07:20] Priya: we can run burst tests and ramp profiles. if you can give us a short timeline of your spike patterns we'll emulate it.
[07:33] Owen: sample integration path — minimal changes: swap openai host, use Redwood SDK or keep openai client with new endpoint, and then add function calls for triage. is that accurate?
[07:41] Samir: exactly. we have a migration guide and a repo with example node/python snippets.
[07:50] Dana: networking — for Dedicated pilot, do you require inbound rules? we need to know firewall specifics.
[07:57] Jared: we'll provide a network diagram. Dedicated commonly uses outbound-only connections from your VPC to our endpoints with peering for Private. we'll list ports and IPs.
[08:10] Lena: success criteria recap? p95 < 600ms for 250-token flows, triage label accuracy >= 88% on your eval set, structured output 99% schema compliance, and cost reasonable vs our current baseline.
[08:25] Jared: yep plus operational metrics: error rate <1% and per-token cost within the target we'll send.
[08:33] Marcus: PT: do you support embeddings + similarity search for incident deduplication?
[08:37] Priya: yes, embeddings are supported via the same API; we can recommend vector index sizes and quantization settings.
[08:45] Owen: any blockers for starting?
[08:47] Dana: security review needs the pack; i will also need the infra contact to coordinate peering.
[08:54] Jared: we'll send the security pack today and schedule the benchmark kickoff for Aug 3rd; priya will run the first runs and share results.
[09:03] Lena: ok last Q about tool/function calling chain: can Redwood call out to our internal runbook microservice?
[09:11] Samir: yes through function-calling you can have the model return the runbook id and then orchestrate a tool call server-side; Redwood supports structured tool responses and can include a tool-calling sample in the demo.
[09:26] Owen: cool. thanks all. next steps again for clarity?
[09:31] Jared: send SOW & pricing, security docs, sample SDK snippets; priya run baseline; customer share prompts; schedule Aug 3rd benchmark kickoff.
[09:41] Lena: great thanks. we'll aim to have prompts and infra contact by next week.
[09:46] Jared: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts. bye.
notes: Transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and minor name mismatches typical of call exports; speakers sometimes overlap and auto-attribution may be imperfect.
